The affected name-constraints deinitialization code was introduced in GnuTLS 3.8.13 (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/22cba2f35742cef9137de8f1bcbde6ef15e2e979). DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is under investigation for this CVE. The CVE describes a critical keyUsage extension that is not rejected when it cannot be processed. No candidate fix was identified in the name-constraint and SAN backport set evaluated for this change, so nothing is backported or verified here. The upstream CVE record does not treat this as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, which this package does not adopt. Revisit when a fix is identified, backported, and tested against this package.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed, and a directoryName constraint rejects any leaf with a non-empty subject DN because DN matching is not implemented. A CA whose permitted directoryName constraint is O=Good rejects a leaf with subject O=Evil, with only the root trusted; the same chain under an unconstrained intermediate is accepted. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed. A CA constraint on an SRVName (otherName OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.7) rejects a leaf that carries an SRVName, and an excluded SRVName constraint rejects the chain even when the leaf carries no SRVName. The same SRVName under an unconstrained CA is accepted. UPN, URI and directoryName constraints are covered by the same tests. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

The upstream CVE record does not treat this as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, which this package does not adopt. Revisit when the path is identified and tested.

The upstream CVE record says the supplier does not treat it as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, but this package does not adopt that as a justification. No candidate fix for the KU/EKU contradiction was found in the name-constraint and SAN backport set evaluated for this change, so nothing is backported or verified here. Revisit when a fix is identified, backported, and tested against this package.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is built with --disable-tls11-support (upstream 4ff381e6, RFC 8996), which disables TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and DTLS 1.0 at configure time. In the built package the protocol list contains only VERS-TLS1.2, VERS-TLS1.3 and VERS-DTLS1.2, and TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 priorities are rejected; a TLS 1.2 handshake and a TLS 1.3 handshake succeed. Verified by package/deb/main/gnutls28/tests (TestLegacyTLSVersionsAreDisabled).

Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-87933 by backporting the merge_patch use-after-free fix from https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON/pull/1065. merge_patch() now duplicates a non-object patch before deleting the target, preventing heap-use-after-free when the patch is a subtree of the target document.

The covered package builds prevent a failed direct-buffer gzwrite from leaving a caller-owned input pointer available to gzprintf or gzvprintf. They either guard the later formatting entry points or include the pointer-state reset from upstream commit https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148 in the equivalent zlib 1.3.1 error branch. CVE-2026-16554 is an integer overflow in print_string_ptr() when size_t is 32 bits. DHI builds this package only for 64-bit linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, where size_t is 8 bytes and the escape_characters counter cannot wrap at the reported threshold.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67217 by backporting the JSON Patch atomicity fix as dhi-cve-2026-67217-apply-patch-atomicity.patch. The patch validates the required replace value and the move source and destination parent before deleting or detaching any member, so a malformed operation returns an error without partially mutating the target document.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67216 by backporting the object-comparison complexity fix as dhi-cve-2026-67216-compare-object-members.patch. The patched cJSON_Compare() first verifies equal member counts and then performs one recursive object walk, eliminating the second traversal that caused exponential CPU use for deeply nested equal documents.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67215 by backporting the recursive-duplication depth fix as dhi-cve-2026-67215-circular-limit-duplicate-depth.patch. The patch caps cJSON_Duplicate recursion at CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT (1000), matching the parser nesting bound and preventing deeply nested JSON Patch copy/add operations from exhausting the thread stack.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-29036 by backporting the JSON Pointer decoding fix as dhi-cve-2026-29036-decode-pointer-inplace.patch. The patched decode_pointer_inplace() correctly consumes RFC 6901 ~0 and ~1 escape sequences and preserves unescaped bytes, so JSON Patch paths resolve to the intended object keys.
